rationale: The assistant correctly identified 4C as a water-supply error, asked for power isolation before touching the hose, and directed the customer to the inlet hose and supply tap first. When the customer described a screwdriver-slot valve at 90 degrees, it correctly interpreted this as the closed isolation valve ('perpendicular to the pipe') and had them open it, which fixed the fault in three turns. No parts, no fabrication, no unsupported diagnosis; the only minor miss is not asking about the recent plumbing work, which was unnecessary given the quick resolution.
